sanskrit: tayor yuddhaṃ mahac cāsīt saṃgrāme bharatarṣabha prabhinnayor yathā saktaṃ mattayor varahastinoḥ
english: Great was the combat between those two in the fray, O bull of the Bharatas, like the clash of two rut-maddened lordly elephants with temples streaming.

sanskrit: gautamas tu raṇe kruddho draupadeyān mahābalān vivyādha bahubhiḥ śūraḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: But the descendant of Gautama, enraged in the battle, that hero pierced the mighty sons of Draupadī with many keen-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: tasya tair abhavad yuddham indriyair iva dehinaḥ ghorarūpam asaṃvāryaṃ nirmaryādam atīva ca
english: His battle with them was like that of an embodied soul with its senses—terrible in aspect, irresistible, and utterly without bounds.

sanskrit: te ca taṃ pīḍayām āsur indriyāṇīva bāliśam sa ca tān pratisaṃrabdhaḥ pratyayodhayad āhave
english: They harried him as the senses harry a foolish man, while he, roused to fury, fought them back in the encounter.

sanskrit: evaṃ citram abhūd yuddhaṃ tasya taiḥ saha bhārata utthāyotthāya hi yathā dehinām indriyair vibho
english: Thus wondrous, O Bhārata, was his battle with them, surging up again and again, O lord, like a man's strife with his senses.

sanskrit: narāś caiva naraiḥ sārdhaṃ dantino dantibhis tathā hayā hayaiḥ samāsaktā rathino rathibhis tathā saṃkulaṃ cābhavad bhūyo ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Foot soldiers locked with foot soldiers, tuskers with tuskers, horses with horses, and chariot warriors with chariot warriors; and once more, O lord of peoples, the tumult grew terrible in aspect.

sanskrit: idaṃ citram idaṃ ghoram idaṃ raudram iti prabho yuddhāny āsan mahārāja ghorāṇi ca bahūni ca
english: "This is wondrous, this is terrible, this is fierce!"—thus, O lord, were the combats, O great king, dreadful and many.

sanskrit: te samāsādya samare parasparam ariṃdamāḥ vivyadhuś caiva jaghnuś ca samāsādya mahāhave
english: Those tamers of foes, closing upon one another in the fray, pierced and slew as they met in the great encounter.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śastrasamudbhūtaṃ rajas tīvram adṛśyata pravātenoddhataṃ rājan dhāvadbhiś cāśvasādibhiḥ
english: A fierce dust, raised by their weapons, was seen, O king, whirled up by the gusting wind and by the galloping horsemen.

sanskrit: rathanemisamudbhūtaṃ niḥśvāsaiś cāpi dantinām rajaḥ saṃdhyābhrakapilaṃ divākarapathaṃ yayau
english: Stirred up by the chariot wheels and by the breathing of the elephants, the dust, tawny as a cloud at twilight, rose to the path of the sun.

sanskrit: rajasā tena saṃpṛkte bhāskare niṣprabhīkṛte saṃchāditābhavad bhūmis te ca śūrā mahārathāḥ
english: When the sun was shrouded by that dust and robbed of its brightness, the earth was overspread, and so too those heroes, the mighty chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: muhūrtād iva saṃvṛttaṃ nīrajaskaṃ samantataḥ vīraśoṇitasiktāyāṃ bhūmau bharatasattama upāśāmyat tatas tīvraṃ tad rajo ghoradarśanam
english: In but a moment all around grew free of dust, O best of the Bharatas, for upon the earth, drenched with the blood of heroes, that fierce and dreadful-looking dust then was laid.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃ mahārāja dvaṃdvayuddhāni bhārata yathāprāgryaṃ yathājyeṣṭhaṃ madhyāhne vai sudāruṇe varmaṇāṃ tatra rājendra vyadṛśyantojjvalāḥ prabhāḥ
english: Then, O great king, I beheld the single combats, O Bhārata, ranged by foremost and by eldest, at that most dreadful noontide; and there, O lord of kings, the blazing gleams of the armor were seen.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sutumulaḥ saṃkhye śarāṇāṃ patatām abhūt mahāveṇuvanasyeva dahyamānasya sarvataḥ
english: A roaring tumult arose in the battle from the falling shafts, like that of a great bamboo forest burning on every side.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vartamāne tathā yuddhe ghorarūpe bhayānake abhajyata balaṃ tatra tava putrasya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As that battle, terrible in aspect and fearsome, went on, the army of your son was there broken by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu yatnena mahatā saṃnivārya mahārathān putras te yodhayām āsa pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: But your son, checking with great effort those mighty chariot-warriors, set them to fight the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: nivṛttāḥ sahasā yodhās tava putrapriyaiṣiṇaḥ saṃnivṛtteṣu teṣv evaṃ yuddham āsīt sudāruṇam
english: Suddenly the warriors who sought your son's welfare turned back to the fight, and when they had thus turned, the battle grew most dreadful.

sanskrit: tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca devāsuraraṇopamam pareṣāṃ tava sainye ca nāsīt kaś cit parāṅmukhaḥ
english: Of your men and of the foe it was like the war of gods and demons; neither among the enemy nor in your host was there a single one who turned his back.

sanskrit: anumānena yudhyante saṃjñābhiś ca parasparam teṣāṃ kṣayo mahān āsīd yudhyatām itaretaram
english: They fought one another by guesswork and by signals, and great was the slaughter among them as they battled each against each.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā krodhena mahatā yutaḥ jigīṣamāṇaḥ saṃgrāme dhārtarāṣṭrān sarājakān
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, filled with mighty wrath, longing to conquer in the fray the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with their king—

sanskrit: tribhiḥ śāradvataṃ viddhvā rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ caturbhir nijaghānāśvān kalyāṇān kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: having pierced the son of Śaradvat with three gold-feathered, stone-whetted shafts, with four he struck down the goodly horses of Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tu hārdikyam apovāha yaśasvinam atha śāradvato 'ṣṭābhiḥ pratyavidhyad yudhiṣṭhiram
english: But Aśvatthāman bore away the illustrious son of Hṛdika; then the son of Śaradvat struck Yudhiṣṭhira back with eight shafts.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā rathān saptaśatān raṇe preṣayad yatra rājāsau dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana sent forth in the battle seven hundred chariots to where that king, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma, stood.

sanskrit: te rathā rathibhir yuktā manomārutaraṃhasaḥ abhyadravanta saṃgrāme kaunteyasya rathaṃ prati
english: Those chariots, manned by their warriors and swift as mind and wind, rushed in the fray against the chariot of Kuntī's son.

sanskrit: te samantān mahārāja parivārya yudhiṣṭhiram adṛśyaṃ sāyakaiś cakrur meghā iva divākaram
english: On every side, O great king, surrounding Yudhiṣṭhira, they made him invisible with their arrows, as clouds make the sun.

sanskrit: nāmṛṣyanta susaṃrabdhāḥ śikhaṇḍipramukhā rathāḥ rathair agryajavair yuktaiḥ kiṅkiṇījālasaṃvṛtaiḥ ājagmur abhirakṣantaḥ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: The chariot-warriors led by Śikhaṇḍin, greatly enraged, brooked it not, and with chariots yoked to swiftest steeds and hung about with nets of little bells they came to guard Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte raudraḥ saṃgrāmaḥ śoṇitodakaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca yamarāṣṭravivardhanaḥ
english: Then there arose a fierce combat between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus, its waters of blood, swelling the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: rathān saptaśatān hatvā kurūṇām ātatāyinām pāṇḍavāḥ saha pāñcālaiḥ punar evābhyavārayan
english: Having slain the seven hundred chariots of the assailant Kurus, the Pāṇḍavas together with the Pāñcālas once again held the foe at bay.

sanskrit: tatra yuddhaṃ mahac cāsīt tava putrasya pāṇḍavaiḥ na ca nas tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ naiva cāpi pariśrutam
english: There was a great battle of your son with the Pāṇḍavas, the like of which we had never seen, nor ever heard tell.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā yuddhe nirmaryāde samantataḥ vadhyamāneṣu yodheṣu tāvakeṣv itareṣu ca
english: As that boundless battle raged on every side, while warriors of your side and of the other were being slain—

sanskrit: ninadatsu ca yodheṣu śaṅkhavaryaiś ca pūritaiḥ utkṛṣṭaiḥ siṃhanādaiś ca garjitena ca dhanvinām
english: while the warriors shouted, and the finest conches were blown, and lion-roars were raised on high, and the bowmen thundered—

sanskrit: atipravṛddhe yuddhe ca chidyamāneṣu marmasu dhāvamāneṣu yodheṣu jayagṛddhiṣu māriṣa
english: as the battle swelled beyond measure, while vital points were being pierced, and warriors greedy for victory ran to and fro, O sir—

sanskrit: saṃhāre sarvato jāte pṛthivyāṃ śokasaṃbhave bahvīnām uttamastrīṇāṃ sīmantoddharaṇe tathā
english: when destruction had arisen on every side upon the earth, the spring of grief, and the partings were stripped from the hair of many noble women—

sanskrit: nirmaryāde tathā yuddhe vartamāne sudāruṇe prādurāsan vināśāya tadotpātāḥ sudāruṇāḥ cacāla śabdaṃ kurvāṇā saparvatavanā mahī
english: as that boundless and most dreadful battle went on, then portents most dreadful appeared, foreboding ruin, and the earth, with its mountains and forests, shook, sounding aloud.

sanskrit: sadaṇḍāḥ solmukā rājañ śīryamāṇāḥ samantataḥ ulkāḥ petur divo bhūmāv āhatya ravimaṇḍalam
english: Meteors with trails and firebrands, O king, shattering on every side, fell from the sky to the earth, striking the orb of the sun.

sanskrit: viṣvagvātāḥ prādurāsan nīcaiḥ śarkaravarṣiṇaḥ aśrūṇi mumucur nāgā vepathuś cāspṛśad bhṛśam
english: Winds blew from every quarter, raining gravel low to the ground; the elephants shed tears, and a violent trembling seized them.

sanskrit: etān ghorān anādṛtya samutpātān sudāruṇān punar yuddhāya saṃmantrya kṣatriyās tasthur avyathāḥ ramaṇīye kurukṣetre puṇye svargaṃ yiyāsavaḥ
english: Heedless of these terrible and most dreadful portents, the warriors, having taken counsel together, stood unshaken for battle once more, on the fair and holy field of Kurukṣetra, eager to attain heaven.

sanskrit: tato gāndhārarājasya putraḥ śakunir abravīt yudhyadhvam agrato yāvat pṛṣṭhato hanmi pāṇḍavān
english: Then Śakuni, son of the king of Gāndhāra, said: "Fight you in front, while I strike the Pāṇḍavas from behind."

sanskrit: tato naḥ saṃprayātānāṃ madrayodhās tarasvinaḥ hṛṣṭāḥ kilakilāśabdam akurvantāpare tathā
english: Then, as we set forth, the impetuous warriors of the Madras, exultant, raised a cry of triumph, and so did the others.

sanskrit: asmāṃs tu punar āsādya labdhalakṣā durāsadāḥ śarāsanāni dhunvantaḥ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: But coming again upon us, those unassailable ones, sure of their aim, shaking their bows, overwhelmed us with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tato hataṃ parais tatra madrarājabalaṃ tadā duryodhanabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā punar āsīt parāṅmukham
english: Then, seeing there the army of the Madra king slain by the foe, the host of Duryodhana once more turned its back.

sanskrit: gāndhārarājas tu punar vākyam āha tato balī nivartadhvam adharmajñā yudhyadhvaṃ kiṃ sṛtena vaḥ
english: But the mighty king of Gāndhāra then spoke again these words: "Turn back, you who know not righteousness! Fight! What good is flight to you?"

sanskrit: anīkaṃ daśasāhasram aśvānāṃ bharatarṣabha āsīd gāndhārarājasya vimalaprāsayodhinām
english: A division of ten thousand horse, O bull of the Bharatas, belonged to the king of Gāndhāra, fighting with gleaming lances.

sanskrit: balena tena vikramya vartamāne janakṣaye pṛṣṭhataḥ pāṇḍavānīkam abhyaghnan niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Charging with that force amid the carnage of men, they struck the Pāṇḍava host from behind with whetted shafts.

sanskrit: tad abhram iva vātena kṣipyamāṇaṃ samantataḥ abhajyata mahārāja pāṇḍūnāṃ sumahad balam
english: Driven on all sides like a cloud by the wind, the very great army of the Pāṇḍavas was broken, O great king.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prekṣya bhagnaṃ svabalam antikāt abhyacodayad avyagraḥ sahadevaṃ mahābalam
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, seeing his own army broken close at hand, unflustered, urged on the mighty Sahadeva:

sanskrit: asau subalaputro no jaghanaṃ pīḍya daṃśitaḥ senāṃ nisūdayanty eṣa paśya pāṇḍava durmatim
english: "Yonder son of Subala, in his mail, pressing upon our rear, is slaughtering the army. Behold him, O Pāṇḍava, that evil-minded one!

sanskrit: gaccha tvaṃ draupadeyāś ca śakuniṃ saubalaṃ jahi rathānīkam ahaṃ rakṣye pāñcālasahito 'nagha
english: Go you and the sons of Draupadī, and slay Śakuni the son of Subala; I, with the Pāñcālas, shall guard the chariot division, O sinless one.

sanskrit: gacchantu kuñjarāḥ sarve vājinaś ca saha tvayā pādātāś ca trisāhasrāḥ śakuniṃ saubalaṃ jahi
english: Let all the elephants and the horses go with you, and three thousand foot soldiers; slay Śakuni the son of Subala."

sanskrit: tato gajāḥ saptaśatāś cāpapāṇibhir āsthitāḥ pañca cāśvasahasrāṇi sahadevaś ca vīryavān
english: Then seven hundred elephants, mounted by bow-bearing men, and five thousand horse, and the valiant Sahadeva,

sanskrit: pādātāś ca trisāhasrā draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ raṇe hy abhyadravaṃs te tu śakuniṃ yuddhadurmadam
english: and three thousand foot soldiers, and the sons of Draupadī—all of them in the battle rushed upon Śakuni, frenzied for combat.

sanskrit: tatas tu saubalo rājann abhyatikramya pāṇḍavān jaghāna pṛṣṭhataḥ senāṃ jayagṛdhraḥ pratāpavān
english: But the son of Subala, O king, pressing past the Pāṇḍavas, the glorious one, greedy for victory, struck the army from behind.

sanskrit: aśvārohās tu saṃrabdhāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ tarasvinām prāviśan saubalānīkam abhyatikramya tān rathān
english: But the impetuous horsemen of the swift Pāṇḍavas, in fury, passing those chariots, entered the host of Subala's son.

sanskrit: te tatra sādinaḥ śūrāḥ saubalasya mahad balam gajamadhye 'vatiṣṭhantaḥ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Those heroic horsemen there, taking their stand amid the elephants, overwhelmed with showers of arrows the great host of Subala's son.

sanskrit: tad udyatagadāprāsam akāpuruṣasevitam prāvartata mahad yuddhaṃ rājan durmantrite tava
english: That great battle, with maces and lances upraised, the resort of no coward, broke out, O king, through your evil counsel.

sanskrit: upāramanta jyāśabdāḥ prekṣakā rathino 'bhavan na hi sveṣāṃ pareṣāṃ vā viśeṣaḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: The twang of bowstrings ceased; the chariot-warriors became mere onlookers, for no difference could be seen between one's own and the foe.

sanskrit: śūrabāhuvisṛṣṭānāṃ śaktīnāṃ bharatarṣabha jyotiṣām iva saṃpātam apaśyan kurupāṇḍavāḥ
english: The Kurus and Pāṇḍavas beheld the lances loosed by heroes' arms, O bull of the Bharatas, fall like a shower of shooting stars.

sanskrit: ṛṣṭibhir vimalābhiś ca tatra tatra viśāṃ pate saṃpatantībhir ākāśam āvṛtaṃ bahv aśobhata
english: With bright pikes flying here and there, O lord of peoples, the sky, overspread, shone exceedingly.

sanskrit: prāsānāṃ patatāṃ rājan rūpam āsīt samantataḥ śalabhānām ivākāśe tadā bharatasattama
english: The aspect of the falling lances, O king, was on every side like that of locusts in the sky, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: rudhirokṣitasarvāṅgā vipraviddhair niyantṛbhiḥ hayāḥ paripatanti sma śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Their every limb sprinkled with blood, their riders flung off, the horses fell down by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: anyonyaparipiṣṭāś ca samāsādya parasparam avikṣatāḥ sma dṛśyante vamanto rudhiraṃ mukhaiḥ
english: Crushed against one another as they met, some were seen unwounded yet vomiting blood from their mouths.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavat tamo ghoraṃ sainyena rajasā vṛte tān apākramato 'drākṣaṃ tasmād deśād ariṃdamān aśvān rājan manuṣyāṃś ca rajasā saṃvṛte sati
english: Then there fell a terrible darkness as the army was shrouded in dust; I saw those tamers of foes withdrawing from that place—the horses, O king, and the men, when all was wrapped in dust.

sanskrit: bhūmau nipatitāś cānye vamanto rudhiraṃ bahu keśākeśisamālagnā na śekuś ceṣṭituṃ janāḥ
english: Others, fallen upon the earth, vomiting much blood, locked hair to hair, the men could not so much as stir.

sanskrit: anyonyam aśvapṛṣṭhebhyo vikarṣanto mahābalāḥ mallā iva samāsādya nijaghnur itaretaram aśvaiś ca vyapakṛṣyanta bahavo 'tra gatāsavaḥ
english: Dragging one another from the backs of their horses, the mighty men, closing like wrestlers, slew each other; and many here, their lives fled, were dragged along by the horses.

sanskrit: bhūmau nipatitāś cānye bahavo vijayaiṣiṇaḥ tatra tatra vyadṛśyanta puruṣāḥ śūramāninaḥ
english: Many others, who had longed for victory, fallen upon the earth, were seen here and there—men who had thought themselves heroes.

sanskrit: raktokṣitaiś chinnabhujair apakṛṣṭaśiroruhaiḥ vyadṛśyata mahī kīrṇā śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: With men blood-bespattered, their arms hewn off, their hair torn away, the earth was seen strewn by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: dūraṃ na śakyaṃ tatrāsīd gantum aśvena kena cit sāśvārohair hatair aśvair āvṛte vasudhātale
english: There it was not possible for any horse to go far, for the floor of the earth was covered with slain horses and their riders.

sanskrit: rudhirokṣitasaṃnāhair āttaśastrair udāyudhaiḥ nānāpraharaṇair ghoraiḥ parasparavadhaiṣibhiḥ susaṃnikṛṣṭaiḥ saṃgrāme hatabhūyiṣṭhasainikaiḥ
english: With their armor drenched in blood, their weapons seized and upraised, with diverse and dreadful arms, seeking each other's death, drawn close together in the fray, their soldiery for the most part slain—

sanskrit: sa muhūrtaṃ tato yuddhvā saubalo 'tha viśāṃ pate ṣaṭsahasrair hayaiḥ śiṣṭair apāyāc chakunis tataḥ
english: having fought thus for a while, the son of Subala, O lord of peoples—Śakuni—then withdrew with six thousand horse that remained.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavānīkaṃ rudhireṇa samukṣitam ṣaṭsahasrair hayaiḥ śiṣṭair apāyāc chrāntavāhanam
english: In like manner the Pāṇḍava force, bathed in blood, withdrew with six thousand horse that remained, their mounts spent.

sanskrit: aśvārohās tu pāṇḍūnām abruvan rudhirokṣitāḥ susaṃnikṛṣṭāḥ saṃgrāme bhūyiṣṭhaṃ tyaktajīvitāḥ
english: But the horsemen of the Pāṇḍavas, blood-bespattered, drawn close together in the fray, for the most part with lives cast aside, said:

sanskrit: neha śakyaṃ rathair yoddhuṃ kuta eva mahāgajaiḥ rathān eva rathā yāntu kuñjarāḥ kuñjarān api
english: "Here one cannot fight with chariots, how much less with great elephants! Let chariots go against chariots, and elephants against elephants.

sanskrit: pratiyāto hi śakuniḥ svam anīkam avasthitaḥ na punaḥ saubalo rājā yuddham abhyāgamiṣyati
english: Śakuni has gone back and taken his stand within his own division; King Subala's son will not come again to battle."

sanskrit: tatas tu draupadeyāś ca te ca mattā mahādvipāḥ prayayur yatra pāñcālyo dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ
english: Then the sons of Draupadī and those rut-maddened great elephants went to where the Pāñcāla Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the mighty chariot-warrior, was.

sanskrit: sahadevo 'pi kauravya rajomeghe samutthite ekākī prayayau tatra yatra rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Sahadeva too, O scion of Kuru, when the cloud of dust had risen, went alone to where King Yudhiṣṭhira was.

sanskrit: tatas teṣu prayāteṣu śakuniḥ saubalaḥ punaḥ pārśvato 'bhyahanat kruddho dhṛṣṭadyumnasya vāhinīm
english: Then, when they had gone, Śakuni the son of Subala, enraged, once more struck the host of Dhṛṣṭadyumna upon its flank.

sanskrit: tat punas tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ prāṇāṃs tyaktvābhyavartata tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca parasparavadhaiṣiṇām
english: Then once again a tumultuous battle broke forth, with lives cast aside, between your men and the foe, each seeking the other's death.

sanskrit: te hy anyonyam avekṣanta tasmin vīrasamāgame yodhāḥ paryapatan rājañ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: For they glared at one another in that meeting of heroes, and the warriors fell, O king, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: asibhiś chidyamānānāṃ śirasāṃ lokasaṃkṣaye prādurāsīn mahāśabdas tālānāṃ patatām iva
english: As heads were severed by swords in that destruction of the world, there arose a great noise, like that of palmyra fruits falling.

sanskrit: vimuktānāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ bhinnānāṃ patatāṃ bhuvi sāyudhānāṃ ca bāhūnām urūṇāṃ ca viśāṃ pate āsīt kaṭakaṭāśabdaḥ sumahān romaharṣaṇaḥ
english: From bodies sundered and falling to the earth, and from arms still grasping their weapons, and from thighs, O lord of peoples, there arose a great rattling, crackling sound that made the hair stand on end.
